# Fresh verification walkthrough — initial findings

Written before any read-only API or implementation inspection. I used browser UI only against the disposable project at http://127.0.0.1:4318. I did not read source, tests, documentation, databases, or application APIs. These are unaltered first-pass findings from an agent inspection, not representative-human validation.

## Outcome and interpretation

I completed all three tasks independently in approximately three minutes of browser task time (20:34:03–20:36:59 UTC, 2026-10-28), with high confidence in the facts visible in the UI. No navigation coaching was needed. Artifact preparation followed the task.

REQ-011 says engineers can distinguish missing statements, allocations, verification plans, changed inputs and unresolved reviews. Its acceptance says each configured queue explains its population and qualifying gap, and structural gaps must not imply failed execution or missing implementation when code may be unlinked.

The original genuine activity records a direct relationship change that should produce one changed input but reported zero. AC-1 failed; AC-2 was not run because the focused assertion stopped the activity. The original failing candidate was acc8b65. The original corrected candidate ef93133 records passes after entity and direct relationship comparisons were counted after edit/removal. A later shared comparison-summary refactor changed support and prompted the currently selected activity, “Current REQ-011 verification after shared comparison refactor.” That activity records both AC-1 and AC-2 passed, with nine unit checks, six production browser journeys, a build, and fifteen lifecycle regressions noted in its conditions. I read these recorded claims; I did not execute them.

The current case says “Verified for this declared scope,” with current governing basis, complete source coverage, zero unassigned criteria, current result selection and zero unassessed activities. The original failure did not disappear: it remains explicitly failed and superseded with changed support. The original corrected pass is also retained as superseded. The selected current activity has no unassessed support change. Historical outcomes remain separate from applicability.

## Separate walkthrough and draft survival

I created “Fresh agent walkthrough REQ-011 — engineering method not run” (case 21f4d418-bbe5-433d-bace-24f286954fed). I deliberately chose the entire acceptance field (characters 0–176), named the combined criterion AC-1-and-AC-2, assigned VER-011 v5, declared complete acceptance coverage, and explained that method assignment is scope clarity, not execution.

I entered the activity “Fresh UI walkthrough — VER-011 not executed” with not_run, explicit conditions identifying browser-only agent inspection, an honest observation and rationale. Before saving I returned to the map and reopened Verification from Project tools. The exact execution conditions and observation survived, including marker FRESH-REQ011-SURVIVES-MAP. I then added REQ-011 v3 as a supporting input with purpose explaining that reading acceptance supports interpretation of not_run, and saved the activity (00379e0a-e5af-4858-8c07-02058fea2012).

I used Choose results to select the only activity and supplied accounting and selection rationales. The case now has current result selection, zero unassessed activities, outcome not_run and current applicability. It remains open. The interface says not every obligation has an applicable passing execution and disables Conclude verification. This is sensible: a current, well-accounted non-execution cannot verify engineering acceptance, and this independent case does not undo the other case’s scoped conclusion.

## Reload and exact context

Reload returned me to the map rather than reopening the task panel. I independently reopened Project tools > Verification, searched “Fresh agent,” selected the saved v3 case, and opened the saved activity. Its original condition, marker, not_run outcome and rationale were present.

Expanded Exact captured inputs shows five records and two connections: MODEL-REQUIREMENT-VERIFICATION native v1 definition; case 21f4d418 native v1 model; REQ-011 native v3 statement and acceptance; VER-011 native v5 method and expectedResult; my explicit REQ-011 native v3 supporting input with its purpose; verified_by v1 declared method mapping; and has_verification_execution v1 owned case-execution membership. This was visible through the UI without API assistance.

## Choices, friction, mistakes and limits

Search made the original failure, correction, case, execution and plan easy to discover together. I first tried Assess evidence, which reasonably sounded like verification but opened generic change assessment. The generic map inspector for the verification case showed connections and history rather than the lifecycle task. I found the dedicated Verification action under Project tools without assistance. The case selector repeats title twice, which adds noise.

The whole-acceptance option was useful for declaring a truthful scope without pretending I had highlighted separate clauses. Combining both AC clauses is deliberate, although separate clauses would produce more granular outcomes. The supporting-input chooser needed opening before its controls were visible. The saved exact-context disclosure made source versions and connection roles inspectable.

The activity detail describes a not_run activity as “Newly performed activity attested with explicit conditions and results.” In context the result remains plainly not_run, but this phrase could sound like the engineering method itself ran. I chose Newly performed activity to describe the actual walkthrough rather than falsely interpret an earlier activity. My conditions explicitly disambiguate that.

I made automation locator mistakes: initially sought a textbox instead of the search combobox; used overly broad combobox/button matches; assumed text line breaks; omitted criterion prefixes on result fields; and guessed an exact-input count of two before reading the actual five. I recovered from visible DOM labels and normal controls. These are agent interaction mistakes, not product failures. No task failed and no passing test was invented.

This single fresh-agent walkthrough supports agent discoverability/comprehension evidence only. It does not validate representative-human usability or the engineering method. I changed only the disposable project through normal UI saves, wrote these reports/screenshots, and did not edit product code or the live project database. No read-only API follow-up was needed.

Screenshots: fresh-current-verification.png; fresh-map-before-save.png; fresh-draft-retained.png; fresh-not-run-accounted.png; fresh-reloaded-exact-context.png.
